history: Fernand Petiot brought his Paris bloody mary to the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis in New York in 1934 and rebuilt it on gin. The hotel still serves it under this name.
whyItWorks: Gin gives the tomato something to argue with. Juniper and celery are a natural pair, which is why this drinks more like a savoury cocktail than a brunch staple.
steps: Build everything in a shaker with ice.
Roll it — pour between two tins three or four times. Do not shake, or the tomato goes frothy.
Garnish with a lemon wedge and a celery stalk.
techniqueNotes: Rolling, not shaking, is the whole technique. A shaken bloody is aerated and thin.
Celery bitters are a modern addition and not in Petiot’s build, but they do the job celery salt was doing.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Savoury and botanical — made for this drink.

substitutions.notes: Celery salt on the rim covers the same ground.
Vodka gives you a Bloody Mary.

name: Red Snapper
description: The gin Bloody Mary — sharper, drier and more aromatic than the vodka version.
creator: Fernand Petiot
